title: Psiaki v. Pacific Northwest Presbytery
disposition_detail: Complaint sustained. The SJC answered “Yes” to whether the CPC Session erred in installing officers elected at the February 5, 2023 congregational meeting despite excluding communing members under 18 from voting; held the complaint judicially in order because it challenged a Session action, not a congregational action; rejected the Presbytery’s BCO 20-3/24-3 “good and regular standing” defense; and ruled the CPC bylaw age restriction unconstitutional. It did not annul the completed ordination/installation, instead requiring future elections and installations to comply with the Constitution. The panel’s proposed denial was replaced by a substitute motion; the final decision was adopted 15-5, with 3 absent and 1 disqualified.
first_summary: The SJC sustained Timothy Psiaki’s complaint against Pacific Northwest Presbytery, holding that Covenant Presbyterian Church’s bylaw excluding communing members under 18 from voting in officer elections violates the BCO. The SJC read BCO 6-4, 25-1, and 25-7 to give all communing members voting rights and rejected the Presbytery’s “good and regular standing” defense. It ordered future elections to comply with the Constitution.
summary: The SJC sustained Psiaki’s complaint and held that the CPC Session erred by ordaining and installing officers elected at a February 5, 2023 congregational meeting where the congregation’s bylaw excluded communing members under 18 from voting. Reading BCO 6-4, 25-1, and 25-7 together, the SJC ruled that all communing members are entitled to vote and that local bylaws cannot impose an age restriction; the “good and regular standing” language addresses censure, not age. The decision did not annul the completed ordination/installation, but required future elections and installations to comply with the Constitution.

evidence_notes.identity_and_adoption: Case No. 2023-11, Mr. Timothy Psiaki v. Pacific Northwest Presbytery, Decision on Complaint dated March 7, 2024, adopted by the SJC. The panel initially proposed denying the complaint; a substitute motion replaced the panel’s issue, judgment, and reasoning, and the final decision was adopted 15-5, with 3 absent and 1 disqualified. Source lines 13–17, 210–214.
evidence_notes.dispute: Complainant alleged the CPC Session installed officers elected at the February 5, 2023 congregational meeting after the CPC bylaws excluded communing members under 18 from voting. The Session rejected and then ruled the complaint out of order; Presbytery ruled it out of order without stated grounds; Psiaki carried it to the General Assembly. Source lines 21–39, 45–48.
evidence_notes.outcomes_and_reasons: The SJC answered the issue “Yes,” held the complaint judicially in order because it challenged a Session action rather than a congregational action, and sustained it. It reasoned that BCO 6-4, 3-1, 16-1/2, 25-1, and 25-7 entitle all communing members to vote, that local bylaws cannot contradict the BCO, and that “good and regular standing” in BCO 20-3/24-3 refers to censure, not age. It did not annul the prior ordination/installation but required future compliance. Source lines 49–208.
evidence_notes.qualifications: The adopted reasoning controls. A separate concurrence agreed with the result but urged a BCO amendment; dissenting opinions argued that local age regulation was permissible. RE Donahoe was disqualified because he belonged to the presbytery. Source lines 210–214, 218–244, 246–489, 491–658.
evidence_notes.incorporated_decisions: The adopted decision distinguishes SJC 2022-20 Wilson v. Pacific Northwest Presbytery, which held a complaint against a congregation’s action judicially out of order. Wilson’s supplied result is used only for that procedural distinction; no other incorporated decision supplies the operative result. Source lines 59–65.
